subject: Eval playback and integration ownership — NexaHealth trial
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Eval playback and integration ownership — NexaHealth trial

Samir — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call recap / proposed success criteria (draft)
- Primary objective: Validate Redwood inference for clinical summarization pipeline at 200 reqs/min under production-like payloads.
- Quality bar: F1 >= 0.88 on the 500-case annotated test set (we'll exchange a redacted sample).
- Latency target: median 150ms/token with 95th <= 500ms for 1–2k token sequences.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 controls + BAA in place for PHI; data preview only, no persistent PHI stored.

Suggested trial scope & timeline
- 5/26: Technical kickoff (SE + infra).
- 5/26–6/09: Integration window — SDK routes, streaming enabled, function/tool-calling for EHR lookups.
- Week of 6/09: Evaluation run and quality metrics collection.
- 6/16: Decision checkpoint (go/no-go / next steps).

Owners (Redwood)
- SE lead / integration: Dev Patel (dev_patel) — SDK, auth, streaming hooks.
- Instrumentation & observability: Marcus Lin (marcus_lin) — dashboards, cost/latency traces.
- Program lead / commercial: Aisha Rahman (aisha_rahman) — cadence, MQA, procurement coordination.

What we need from NexaHealth
- Redacted sample dataset (500 cases) by 5/24 to run the initial quality pass.
- A test API account and EHR sandbox details for function/tool-calling (FHIR endpoints and auth method).
- Confirmation on whether trial will include PHI in transit (we recommend PII redaction during trial).

Attachments included: nexa_poc_success_criteria.xlsx (draft success criteria).

If that looks right I’ll schedule the kickoff for 5/26 and loop in our compliance lead for SOC2/BAA questions.

Thanks —
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com] | +1 (415) 555-0198

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Eval playback and integration ownership — NexaHealth trial

Thanks Aisha — adding a bit more color from the SE side so Nexa’s engineers have a concrete plan to review. I’ve quoted Aisha’s success criteria below and added technical checks.

> Call recap / proposed success criteria (draft)
> - Primary objective: Validate Redwood inference for clinical summarization pipeline at 200 reqs/min under production-like payloads.

Technical integration plan (high-level)
- Auth & networking:
  - We support API key auth (long-lived) and short-lived mTLS tokens for the Private deployment. For trial, we'll provide a sandbox API key scoped to the trial project.
  - Recommend a direct peered link or TLS-only traffic via our hosted region (we can discuss VPC peering if you want private connectivity).
- SDK & routes:
  - SDK (Python/Node) has an out-of-the-box route: /v1/generate/stream for streaming token-by-token output.
  - For batch evaluation, use /v1/generate/batch with a 100–500 request batching window (we'll tune for latency).
- Streaming and KV caching:
  - We'll enable prefix caching for repeated prompts (saves 30–60% tokens for clinical templates).
- Function / tool calling (FHIR lookups):
  - Redwood supports structured function-calling. We'll model a FHIR getPatientSummary function that triggers a validated webhook to your EHR sandbox.
  - Recommended pattern: Redwood invokes function -> EHR returns structured JSON (FHIR) -> model consumes JSON to produce final summary.
- Observability & test harness:
  - Marcus will provision dashboards (latency by route, token counts, error rates) and a short-lived trace for the first 48 hours.
- Estimated SE effort & timeline:
  - Kickoff (half-day) + 4 engineering days (SE + Nexa engineer) to wire SDK + function callbacks.
  - Instrumentation and initial evaluation: 2 days.

Required from Nexa engineers to unblock:
- Sandbox FHIR endpoint + documentation (OpenID/OAuth details if any).
- CORS/ingress allowlist for our sandbox IPs (we can provide ranges).
- Sample payloads and typical sequence length distribution (avg/max tokens).

I attached an integration_checklist.md that lays these items out as a short runbook. If Nexa prefers, we can convert the checklist into a shared Google Doc during the kickoff.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[dev_patel@redwoodinference.com]

--
[attachment: integration_checklist.md]

From: Samir Gupta <samir@nexahealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@nexahealth.com
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval playback and integration ownership — NexaHealth trial

Aisha / Dev — thanks for the clear plan. A few quick notes from our side: 

1) Data sample: we can provide a de-identified 500-case sample by 2027-05-24 as requested. Will deliver CSV + small JSON set.
2) FHIR/tool-calling: yes, we want the model to make calls back to our sandbox (FHIR R4). Important: the payloads may include limited PHI in transit. We need to confirm your retention policy and whether data persists in logs.
3) Compliance: please share SOC2 report and typical BAA language up front. Procurement is on a tight timeline — if we can get a draft agreement this week, procurement can triage.
4) Timeline: 5/26 kickoff sounds good. Can we do 10:00am PT? Our dev lead (Priya Shah) will join.

Other question: does Redwood support on-the-fly rerouting to a smaller quantized model if we see cost/latency issues during the run? We’ll want an automated fallback path if throughput spikes.

Thanks —
Samir Gupta
VP Product, NexaHealth
samir@nexahealth.com

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@nexahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@nexahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 08:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Eval playback and integration ownership — NexaHealth trial

Samir — great, appreciate the quick turnaround. Short answers and next steps below.

1) SOC2 / BAA: attaching our latest SOC2 summary (redwood_soc2_report.pdf) and I’ve asked legal to prepare a BAA draft and push to the DocuSign link below. We do not persist raw PHI in the hosted trial by default; logs are redacted and retention is configurable.
2) Function calling & PHI in transit: we support structured function-calling with callback webhooks. For PHI, we recommend Private deployment or VPC-peered sandbox for the trial; if you need hosted trial, we will enable mTLS and token scoping plus redaction hooks.
3) Fallback routing / quantized models: yes — our smart routing policy can fail over to a smaller quantized model variant automatically when latency or cost thresholds are exceeded. We’ll configure a canary policy during the evaluation.

Confirmed items / actions
- Nexa: deliver data sample (500 de-identified cases) by 5/24 — Samir / Priya.
- Redwood: SOC2 + BAA draft to Samir & procurement by EOD 5/20 — Aisha.
- Kickoff: 5/26 @ 10:00am PT — Dev to run SDK walkthrough; Marcus to review dashboards. Meeting invite to follow.
- SE tasks pre-kickoff: provide sandbox API key, IP ranges, and integration_checklist doc — Dev (by 5/21).

Links / attachments
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345
- SOC2 summary: https://redwood-docs.internal/soc2 (attached redwood_soc2_report.pdf)
- DocuSign draft BAA: https://na.docusign.net/XYZ-NEA-draft

If that all looks good I’ll send the calendar invite and loop in legal/procurement. Thanks everyone — looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
